answer: Pay each agent only its leave-one-out delta. Questions resolve later, so the network can rerun the aggregate forecast without one identity and see how much accuracy drops. An independent agent adds its own signal, so removing it moves the score. A farm of clones repeats one model's view, so dropping any single sparrow from the flock barely changes anything while its twins carry the same answer, and each clone earns near zero. Spinning up more personas splits the reward instead of multiplying it.
